qualification: Qualitative review only; no physical or photometric F135 calibration.

videos.title: How The World's Most Powerful Fighter Jet Engine Is Made
videos.publisher: Sam Eckholm; description credits Pratt & Whitney sponsorship
observations: A contracted nozzle is visible at 720 s.
Pink/violet external emission is visible at 760, 810 and 820 s.
limitations: Storyboard samples, not measured spectra or synchronized engine telemetry.
Video includes discussion of multiple variants; no PW-600 nozzle control calibration established.

videos.title: Back in the game - Flying the F-35 from HMS Queen Elizabeth
videos.publisher: Navy Lookout; description credits Royal Navy video by LPhot Dan Shepherd
observations: At158s a red/orange external trail is visible behind the nozzle.
At161s the aircraft is in the ski-jump ramp shot; the vertical-landing close-up follows around162.8s.
At162.8s a downward nozzle, external luminous region and bright deck patch are clearly visible.
The current simulator does not reproduce the reported non-AB powered-lift appearance.
limitations: No augmentation telemetry. Manufacturer states hover uses no afterburner; footage is not proof of AB in hover.
Pixels do not separate gas/particle self-emission from scattered/reflected light or heated deck emission.
Exposure, white balance, camera curve and grading are unknown.
videos.method: 1080p video extract requested from 156 to 163 s; individual frames sought at relative 2, 5, 6 and 6.8 s. Timestamps are approximate to a video frame.

videos.title: Amazing Back View! at Afterburner Take-Off - F-35A, F-15E, F-16 and EA-18G
videos.publisher: USA Military Channel; credits U.S. Air Force footage
observations: The first 111 s identifies F-35A, not F-35B.
Rear-view sequence shows a bright annular region with a darker center and nonuniform brightness.
User identifies eight bright spots at 92 s; reviewer cannot independently resolve the exact count in the small, distorted nozzle image.
limitations: Eight-spot count remains a hypothesis, not hardware identification.
Heat shimmer, pixel resolution, exposure and perspective limit spatial measurement.
Brightness does not measure velocity or identify flameholder/spraybar count.
videos.method: 1080p video extract requested from 90 to 94 s; inspected 92 s and half-second samples across the interval.

primarySources.supports: F135-PW-600 augmented two-spool layout; component stage counts.
Designer distinguishes a historic deflected-AB ground rig from operational X-35B/F-35B hover without AB; also documents cooling and nozzle variants.
Swivel module supports afterburning in conventional flight.
A8/A9 control and compact STOVL versus CTOL/CV nozzle.
Jet-fuel CH/C2 bands and soot-continuum mechanisms; not F135 weights.
Main-combustor liner radiation/convection/film-cooling example; corrects earlier mislabel as an afterburner-liner experiment.
N1/N2 identify rotor speeds, not temperatures.
Whitebalance/tint, exposure and clipping affect rendered photographs; no recovery of missing camera calibration claimed.
Main burner and downstream afterburner are separate stations.
Experimental downstream ring flameholders and discrete mixers establish possible spatial mechanisms, not F135 hardware identity or an eight-spot count.
Recirculating flameholder wakes stabilize combustion; a bright region does not establish fastest axial flow.

openDiscrepancies: Full-resolution powered-lift close-up confirms light outside the downward nozzle and on the deck; current non-AB exhaust/deck-light appearance is incomplete.
Dry 99% metal heats but remains almost dark with the assumed cooled single region.
Soot-biased warm gas profile does not represent all observed F135 hues.
Nozzle authored minimum and generic N2 schedule are uncalibrated.
Flat interior cap and uniform thermal region omit spatial features seen in the rear-view video.
